name: Question 14
problem:
The matrix $C$ and the vector $b$ are given below.
Determine if $b\in \text{Col}(C).$ 
In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers such that $b={x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}+{x}_{3}{c}_{3},$ and ${c}_{1}$, ${c}_{2}$, and ${c}_{3}$ are the respective columns of $C.$

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -12 \\ -6\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
In order to determine whether $b$ lies in $\text{Col}(C),$ we need to check if the equation $Cx=b$ is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix $[C\,|\,b]$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[C\,|\,b] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 & -8 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & -12 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 & -8 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & -12 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 3 & -8 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & -12 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-8 \\ 2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=-12 \\ 5{x}_{3}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting it into the second equation gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-(2) & =-12 \\ {x}_{2} & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, from the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-8-3{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\  & =-8-3(-5)-3(2) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we have a solution, the equation $Cx=b$ is consistent, which implies that $b\in \text{Col}(C).$ 

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${c}_{1},$ ${c}_{2},$ and ${c}_{3}:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -12 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}=1\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{1}}+(-5)\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{2}}+2\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{c}_{3}}
$$

Finally, we get ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=1\cdot (-5)\cdot 2=-10.$

EXPLANATION

In order to determine whether b lies in Col(C), we need to check if the equation Cx=b is consistent. So, let's find the row echelon form of the augmented matrix [C|b] as follows:

[C|b]=[133−802−1−12−110−6]R3:=R3+R1∼[133−802−1−12043−14]R3:=R3−2R1∼[133−802−1−1200510]

Now, we have the system

{x1+3x2+3x3=−82x2−x3=−125x3=10.

From the third equation, we get x3=2. Substituting it into the second equation gives

2x2−(2)=−12x2=−5.

Finally, from the first equation, we get

x1=−8−3x2−3x3=−8−3(−5)−3(2)=1.

Since we have a solution, the equation Cx=b is consistent, which implies that b∈Col(C).

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write b as a linear combination of c1, c2, and c3:

[−8−12−6]⏟b=1⋅[10−1]⏟c1+(−5)⋅[321]⏟c2+2⋅[3−10]⏟c3

Finally, we get x1⋅x2⋅x3=1⋅(−5)⋅2=−10.
